text:
name: monthly_spending_check
does: Gives a quiet, short summary of what a person spent this month in each group, like food or bills, and how much is left.
inputs: the month, and the spending groups to look at
people say:
- How much have I spent on food?
- Am I over my budget this month?
- Where did my money go?
- I need to know what is left for the rest of the week.
- I am a bad cook so we eat out a lot, what did that cost?

name: pick_wash_cycle
does: Chooses the right washing machine setting for a load of clothes.
inputs: what the clothes are made of, how dirty they are, and how long you have
people say:
- My sister and I share one machine, what setting for her silk shirt and my socks?
- Will a hot wash shrink these jeans?
- How much does it cost to use cold water compared to warm?
- I have towels and sheets, which program is best?
- Fast wash, I need these dry by noon.

Walt was not good with technology, and his computer made him nervous. His grandfather had given him the machine and always said it was easy, but Walt did not agree. One morning the words on his screen looked too small, and he was in a hurry. He typed to the assistant: incrase the text size on my screen. The assistant understood what he meant, despite the typo, and increased the text size. Walt was pleased. He then asked it to remind him every week to save his files, and the assistant set a weekly reminder for Sunday at ten. Walt said thanks and went back to work, with the big letters easy to read.

name: resume_audiobook
does: Opens the audiobook or podcast where you stopped and plays it at the speed you like.
inputs: the title and the speed, if you want one
people say:
- Where was I in the book my uncle gave me?
- Keep going from last night.
- Play the heavy history book from where I stopped.
- Can you divide the long book by chapters and start at the next one?
- Slow it down, he talks too fast.

Things at home wear out, and a repair is easier when you plan it. A filter in a heater or a fan needs a change every few months. People say, remind me to change the filter every three months. If something breaks, they say, book a plumber for Thursday, and they tell the shop what is wrong, such as the depth of the water under the sink, or where the leak started. Someone with a broken favourite kettle might say, find me a repair shop near home.

A reminder helps you put the job on the calendar. You can change it with words like, make it earlier, or move it to next month.

Person: hey, play the lovley garden podcast
Assistant: That is a lovely show. Which episode do you want? The newest one, or one you listened to before?
Person: the one about how to chop roots
Assistant: I found an episode about pruning roots and vegetables. Is that the one?
Person: yes. also put a cherry tree one on after
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't line up more than one episode right now. I can play the root episode first, and you can ask for the cherry tree one when it ends.
Person: ok fine

name: power_cut_help
does: Tells you what to do when the lights go out and helps you find out if neighbors have the same problem.
inputs: your address, and what you can see, like no lights or a flickering fuse
people say:
- All the power just went out.
- I'm nervous, it's dark and I can't find a flashlight.
- Where did I put my tool belt with the torch in it? It's pitch black.
- Search for news about a blackout in my area.
- Is it only my house, or the whole street?
- Tell me what to do with the food in the fridge.

name: parking_timer
does: Keeps track of how long you can stay in a parking spot and tells you before time runs out.
inputs: how long you paid for, and where you parked
people say:
- I paid for two hours, tell me before it ends.
- Set a reminder to move the car at three.
- I parked on the purple level, near the stairs.
- How much time is left on the meter?
- Don't let me get a ticket.
- Help me unpack the groceries, then tell me when it's time to go.

name: tell_my_people
does: Sends a short message to chosen family or neighbors when something goes wrong, so they can warn others or come help.
inputs: who to tell, and what happened
people say:
- let my wife know I'm at the clinic, my tooth got knocked out
- send a polite note to the neighbors, the water is rising in the street
- please warn the family that the power is out
- message my brother that there is smoke in the kitchen
- everybody on my safety list needs to know I'm fine

Ana had just moved to the city, and she was in a small cafe on a rainy afternoon. She had a stale cookie and a good book, and she wanted to spend the afternoon reading. She said to her phone, "Resume book." The assistant understood that she wanted to continue her audiobook, and it started it at chapter nine, right where she had stopped. A few minutes later she asked, "Time left?" The assistant said the chapter had twenty minutes to go, and the length of the whole book was about four hours. Ana smiled and said, "Bookmark here." The assistant saved the spot.

Priya had just woken up when she heard a drip in the bathroom. She sat up in bed and said to her phone, "Excuse me, could you please check if water is running anywhere in the house? I heard a strange drip in the night and I am worried about the pipes." The assistant understood she wanted a leak check. It looked at the water meter, which was still moving even though no tap was open. The assistant told her this might mean a leak, maybe in the pipe that connects the sink to the wall. It offered to shut off the main water valve, and Priya said yes. The assistant closed it and said the chicken in the sink would have to wait for fresh water. Priya laughed and called a plumber.

Arithmetic is the part of math we use every day. We learn it in the very first lesson at school. We add numbers to see how much we have, take them away to see what is left, multiply to find the total of equal groups, and divide to share things. People use it when they shop, cook or split a bill. They ask for it in many ways. Some say what is twelve and eight, others say take five off thirty, or share a hundred between four. If you make a mistake, you can say start again or restart from zero. A big sum may be hard to do in your head, so many people simply ask a phone. It gives the answer in a second.

Kai was walking home from school with a package under one arm. A little earlier, his friends had taken a funny picture of a puppy on a skateboard. They joked that it would grow into a huge dog and never fit on the board again. Kai wanted to send the picture, but both hands were full, so he spoke to his phone.

He typed in a hurry, 'send the last pic to mom and to my frends.'

The assistant understood who he meant by mom and found the newest photo in his gallery. It showed the photo of the puppy and asked, 'Is this the one?'

'Yes,' said Kai. The assistant sent it to his mom and to the group chat called Friends. Kai felt calm. He would not have to stop in the street. Soon his phone buzzed with laughing faces.

Person: Can you make the sprinklers run more this week?
Assistant: Sure. Which ones, the front yard or the back yard?
Person: The back yard. I help my mom with her garden and the grass looks dry.
Assistant: They run ten minutes each morning now. How much more do you want?
Person: Double it please.
Assistant: Done. They will run twenty minutes every morning.
Person: Can you scroll down and show me where the broken one is?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't see the sprinklers or find a broken one. I can put it on your to-do list so you remember to check the heads.
Person: Yes, do that.

Person: I need to pay the electric bill.
Assistant: I can help with that. Which bill is it, and how much is it?
Person: Twenty-five dollars. I'm very tired after work, so please be quick.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't pay bills. But I can remind you of the date and the amount.
Person: That's fine. It's due on the tenth. I just bought some pork on the way home, and I forgot the date. Can you zoom in on the bill photo so I can read it?
Assistant: Yes, I zoomed in. It is due on the tenth. Should I remind you the day before?
Person: Yes, please. I got a message saying it was late, but that was a false alarm.
Assistant: Good. I'll remind you on the ninth.

Jess, a teenager, was learning to cook noodles while texting her friends. Her phone showed twenty-five missed calls, all from her grandmother. That was strange, so she said, "Call Grandma back on speaker." The assistant understood that she wanted to ring her grandmother and use the speakerphone so her hands stayed free. The call started. Grandma was in the attic, looking through old boxes on a cloudy afternoon, and her phone had been on silent. "I found your dad's baby photos," she said, laughing. Jess turned down the heat under the pot, read a quick message from a friend, and asked Grandma to hold up the pictures. The assistant kept the call going on speaker the whole time.

The person wants to know the score of tonight's match.
What's the score?
Who's winning?
Did the Reds win?
Tell me how my team is doing, it's been twenty minutes since I checked.
Is the match over yet, or are they still playing?
I'm cutting a carrot for dinner and can't look, so what's the score?
Dinner is cooked and I'm not watching, so what's the score?
I'm going to chill on the couch, so just tell me when someone scores.
Did the Reds win by more than twenty-five points? Wait, I mean the Blues.

name: world_clock
does: Tells you what time it is in another city, with an automatic check for summer and winter clock changes, so you know if it is too late to call.
inputs: the name of a city
people say:
- What time is it in Tokyo?
- Is it morning in Lima yet?
- Pull up the time in Paris.
- It's six here. Is it too late to call the boiler company in Chicago?
- Time in New York right now?

Kai was running out the door with his bag half open and his desk messy. "Put bake the cake on my list for today, but don't put it before the dentist, I'll never make it," he said to his phone. "And tell me what's left." The assistant added "bake the cake" to the end of the list, after the dentist visit. Then it read out the three things still to do: buy eggs, call his friend Jo about her party, and pick up the mail. Kai nodded, locked the door, and ran for the bus.

Scaling a recipe means making more or less of a dish than the card says. My grandma makes a soup that serves four, but if you have eight guests, you need double. Cups, spoons and servings all change together. People say, make it for six, cut it in half, or I only need enough for one. The numbers change: two cups of rice become four, and a half spoon of salt becomes a whole one. Some people also say, wake me up when the soup is ready, and set a timer. It helps when the recipe uses cups but your measuring tool uses spoons, because the helper can change one to the other.

Person: Play podcast.
Assistant: Sure. Which podcast do you want?
Person: the cooking one, the crispy chicken show
Assistant: Found it. Do you want the newest episode, or where you stopped last time?
Person: where i stopped. i have to split it, half before the school run and half after
Assistant: Okay. I'll play from minute twenty-two. Tell me when to stop and I will save your place.
Person: thanks, you're the best

name: check_water_temperature
does: Tells you how warm the sea or pool water is by reading a network of sensors near the beach.
inputs: the beach or pool name, and the time if it is not now
people say:
- Is the water too cold to swim?
- Can the kids go in without a wetsuit?
- Talk me through how warm the sea is today
- What is the temperature at the pool?
- Turn on the automatic warning if the lake gets warmer than yesterday

Ana, an office worker, sat down in the dim office on a Monday morning and her nose began to itch. The highway outside was busy and the air smelled like smoke. She began to speak to her assistant. 'Turn on the air purifier and close the window by my desk,' she said, 'because I can't breathe well.' The assistant understood that she wanted two things in one go. It switched on the purifier at a medium speed and shut the smart window beside her desk. Then it said, 'The purifier is running. I closed the window.' After a few minutes the air felt fresh and Ana began her work.

Someone wants a bike route that is about twenty-five kilometres long.
Plan a ride that is around twenty-five kilometres.
I want to ride for about an hour and a half.
Show me a loop that gets me back home after a good long ride.
I hate hills, so keep it flat, and about the same length as last Saturday.
It's a crispy cold morning and I want a ride that fills the time before lunch.
Give me a number of kilometres that is not too short and not too long.
Could you please suggest a route of about twenty-five kilometres? I want to get ready for the charity ride next month.

Mrs. Lee, a retired teacher, sat at the kitchen table with a pile of bills. She said to her tablet, "Tell me how much I have spent this month, and remind me to pay the electric bill tomorrow at noon." The assistant added up her spending and said it was nine hundred dollars, with the largest part going to her grandson's drum lessons. It then set a reminder for tomorrow at noon. Mrs. Lee frowned at first, but then she smiled. "It's true," she said, "he plays very well, and I like to pay for it." She put the bills into a neat stack and went to make some tea.

name: spell_word
does: Shows the correct spelling of a single word and says it out loud, one letter at a time.
inputs: the word, and the language if it is not English
people say:
- How do I write hat in Spanish?
- How do you spell paint in French?
- Spell that last word for me, slowly.
- I always get this one wrong, can you check it?
- What letters are in the French word for apple?

Tom was a gardener, and he wore grey gloves all day. In his lunch break he sat on a bench and spoke to his phone. Show me only the unread emails, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to skip the old ones, so it listed just five unread emails. One of them said a package was on its way, but the sender wanted to push the date back. Tom said, read that one, and the assistant read it out loud. Then he said, tell Dana the package will come half an hour later, and the assistant wrote a short email to Dana and asked, shall I send it? Tom said yes. The assistant sent the email, and Tom went back to his roses.

Chen was in a hurry to leave the house, but the rooms were cold. He said to the thermostat, set the heat to twenty-two degrees. Then he thought about the cost of heating a house. It was expensive in winter, and his office was a long distance away, so he would be gone all day. No, make it twenty, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted to fix the number, so it changed the temperature to twenty degrees. Chen also did not want the heat to run all day. He asked it to turn the heating off at eight, and to pick it up again at five. The assistant set both times. Then Chen picked up his bag and went out.

Fatima was making soup when she heard a drip in the west corner of the kitchen. "Excuse me, assistant, could you please help me? I think the pipe under the sink is leaking, and I have a big dinner to cook tonight, and the size of the crowd is forty people, so I need to know if I can still use the water," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted to check her water use for a leak. It said the water meter showed a steady flow even though no tap was on, which usually means a leak. The pot could sit on the stove while she waited. The assistant offered to book a plumber for the afternoon, Fatima said yes, and a plumber was booked for two o'clock.

Person: Take a picture of my screen with this recipe on it and send it to my husband.
Assistant: Done, I have the picture. Should I send it as a message or by email?
Person: A message. And write "can you buy these" under it.
Assistant: Sent with that note. Anything else?
Person: Yes, put the photos from Lucy's party in a new album and share it with Grandma.
Assistant: I can make the album. Which photos, and from which day?
Person: Saturday's. The kids were calm for once.
Assistant: I found 24 photos from Saturday. I made an album called Lucy's party and sent the link to Grandma.

A robot vacuum is a small, round machine that cleans the floor by itself. It is low in height, so it can slide under a chair, but it cannot climb stairs, so it needs a flat floor. People set a cleaning schedule, like every morning at nine, and ask for a different power, such as low, medium or strong. They say "start cleaning," "clean the kitchen only," "stop, I have guests," or "go back to your base." It is a good idea to tidy cables and toys first. When you invite friends over, you might ask it to do a quick extra round before they arrive.

Priya, an office worker, came home tired and saw the electric bill on the table. She was careful with money, so she spoke politely to the smart speaker. "Could you please show me how much electricity we used this week, because I think the heater uses too much and I would like to find out before the bill gets bigger?" The assistant said it understood she wanted her power use for the last seven days and a hint about the heater. It found the numbers and told her the heater had used nearly half of all the power. Priya wondered if an old wire behind the TV was wasting power too. The assistant could not see wires, but it offered to deliver a short report every Monday. Priya said yes, and then asked it to remind her to turn the heater down at ten o'clock.

A podcast is a show you listen to, with a new episode every week. An audiobook is a book read aloud and split into chapters. Both remember where you stopped, so you can pick up again later. Many apps have an automatic setting that moves to the next episode. People listen while they cook, drive or walk, and sometimes a grandfather listens in the garden. To control it, they say, play the next episode, go back thirty seconds, or skip this chapter. If a voice is too slow, they say, play it faster, or one and a half times speed. If they swipe the wrong thing on the phone, they can say, take me back to where I was.

Maya had just woken up and her head was still foggy. Coffee was her morning fuel, but the kettle was not on yet. She looked at her phone and said, "Good morning. I am sorry to ask so early, but could you please look at my calendar and tell me what I have today? I have a new job, and I do not want to be late for my first meeting." The assistant understood that she wanted her day read to her. It began to search her calendar and found two events: a team meeting at nine and lunch with a friend at one. Maya sat up. She thanked the assistant and got out of bed.

Mrs. Bell was not good with her phone. A message popped up that said the storage was full. She spoke to it. "Please help me. I need to make room for photos of my grandchildren." The assistant understood that she wanted to free up space. It filtered her videos to show only the old ones, and found twenty-five that she had not opened for a year. It asked if she wanted to delete them, and she said yes. One was a video of a humid summer day at the beach, but she knew she had a plan to keep the photos safe. The assistant cleared the space, and Mrs. Bell smiled.

Bread rises because yeast makes tiny bubbles in the dough. Bakers wait until the dough is twice as big, then put it in a hot oven. People change a recipe by asking for more time, a hotter oven, or a smaller loaf. They say things like let it rise for another half hour, bake it ten minutes longer, or set the oven to two hundred degrees. In a small flat with a cold kitchen, you may need to organize a warm spot for the dough, such as the downstairs bathroom, a place near a radiator, or a sunny balcony. A timer helps, and an assistant can set one when you say wake me when the dough is ready.

name: recipe_scaler
does: Changes the amounts in a recipe to fit the number of people you are cooking for.
inputs: the recipe, and how many servings you want
people say:
- Make this recipe for six instead of four
- I only have half a block of butter, shrink it
- I can't afford all that cheese, so halve it
- Double the soup for tonight as a temporary change, don't save it
- How many cups is two hundred and fifty grams of flour?

name: ride_status
does: Tells you where your booked ride is and how many minutes until it arrives.
inputs: the ride you booked
people say:
- Where is my taxi?
- How long until the car gets here?
- Is the driver close yet?
- I'm waiting in the heat, how long now?
- I'm in a remote spot, is the pin on the map true, or is the driver lost?

A baby does best with a steady day. Feeding times and nap times help a tiny baby know what comes next. Parents often keep a simple list: milk at seven, nap at nine, milk again at eleven. When the baby is hungry sooner, they say, 'Move the next feed earlier.' When the baby sleeps longer, they say, 'Push the nap later.' A baby monitor lets a parent hear or see the baby from another room. On a morning with thick fog, when the whole house is still, a parent might ask, 'Keep the sound low but let me hear if she cries.' Small changes are made with words like sooner, later, louder and quieter.

A time zone is a part of the world where all the clocks show the same hour. When you travel, or call a friend far away, the time can be very different. A huge number of people check the clock on their phone to see what time it is in another city. The phone knows where you are and sets the time by itself, so one wrong guess cannot plant a seed of trouble, and you do not have to cough up the answer from memory. People say things like, 'What time is it in Tokyo?' or 'Is it morning for my sister in Lima?' If you move to a new place, you can say, 'Change my clock to local time.' Some people also ask for a second clock, to see home and away at once.

People count days all the time. You might want to know how many days are left until a birthday, a holiday or the end of school. You might read the date in a newspaper, or want to know how old someone is, or how many eggs are left in the fridge. A phone can do the counting for you. You choose a start day and an end day, or you give it a thing to count. Some people hate counting by hand, and a few get angry when the number is wrong. To change the answer, people say things like, 'Count from Monday instead,' 'Leave out the weekends,' or 'Add one more day.' Then the new number appears.

name: choose_vacuum_zone
does: Tells a robot vacuum which room or part of a room to clean and when to start, and it can download a new floor map that shows each cleaned area in a different color when the house changes.
inputs: the room or area, the time to start, and how strong the cleaning should be
people say:
- The kitchen floor is a mess, can you clean it now?
- Send the little robot to the hallway.
- Don't do the bedroom today, keep the door open for the cat.
- Run the vacuum every day at noon in the living room.
- Crumbs everywhere under the table, please sort it out.

Person: Start a timer for the game.
Assistant: Sure. How long should the timer run?
Person: Twenty-five minutes. I just got home from the night shift and I want a small game with my kids before I sleep. It is the one where we buy things at a toy market.
Assistant: Okay, a timer for twenty-five minutes. Do you want a sound at the end?
Person: Yes, a soft one. And can you tell me the score of the match last night?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't see the score of your game, because I don't know the numbers. If you tell me, I can keep them.
Person: Okay, I'll say them out loud. Clear the old score too.
Assistant: Done. The old score is cleared and the timer is running.

They want the curtains to be closed.
close the curtains
shut the blinds pls
curtains closed, thx
the sun is in my eyes
It's too bright in here, could you do something with the soft curtains?
can you pull the blinds half way down, I'm about to stretch out and watch a movie and dont want any glare
close them, no wait, just the left window
Could you please close all the shutters? The neighbors can see in and I would like some privacy.

Writing a letter or a story usually begins with a rough draft. You put down your ideas first, and you fix the words later. A phone or computer can do the checking for you. It can fix spelling, count the words and read the text back. Even a person with a sore tooth can write a note to the dentist this way. If an email asks for you to reply by tonight, you can do it fast. To change what you wrote, people say, 'Make it shorter,' 'Use simpler words,' 'Fix my spelling,' 'Sound more polite' or 'How many words is this?' The text then changes. You can always say, 'Go back to the first version,' and your old words return, no matter how tall the pile of drafts.

Greg works in an office and his day is always busy. On Monday he had a big meeting at nine, and he was afraid he would be late. At his desk he said to the speaker, 'Set an alarm for tomorrow at seven, and call it Meeting.' The assistant understood that he wanted a morning alarm with a name. It also noticed a timer already running, one that Greg had set for his lunch. It said, 'Your seven o'clock alarm called Meeting is set. The timer for lunch is still on.' Greg closed the zipper of his bag and went home. The next day the alarm rang right on time.

Person: Good morning. I'm very sorry to ask so early, but my grandson is coming after school and I will be out, so could you unlock the front door for him at four?
Assistant: Of course. Do you want it to stay unlocked, or lock again after he comes in?
Person: Please lock it again after about ten minutes.
Assistant: Okay. The front door will unlock at four and lock at ten past. Do you also want to give him a code?
Person: Yes. Also, can you sell my old key to the shop on the corner?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't sell things. I can tell you which shop is closest. Would you like to open the camera channel to see the most recent visits at your door?
Person: That would be nice, thank you.

They want to know when a film is showing at the cinema.
What time is the film on?
When does the new space movie start?
Showtimes for tonight, please.
I'm making dinner and I'll heat some creamy pasta first, so tell me when the film begins.
Set a reminder for what's showing at the cinema tomorrow at seven.
Any good films on this weekend?
Could you check the cinema and tell me the times for the funny one with the dog?
Is there a late show?
I'd love to see something after work, so what is playing and when?

name: car_status_check
does: Updates you on the fuel level and the tyre pressure of the car.
inputs: which car, if there is more than one
people say:
- Do I have enough fuel for the drive on Saturday?
- Is the car ready for a short trip to the shops?
- Are my tyres okay?
- How much petrol is left?
- Is anything wrong with the car?

Person: Play the radio.
Assistant: Which station would you like?
Person: The kids one with the funny songs.
Assistant: Okay, playing Kids Fun Radio. Is the volume all right?
Person: Yes, it's a lovely song. What is the date of the next funny show? Can you record it tomorrow at seven?
Assistant: The next show is on Friday. I'm sorry, I can't record radio shows. I can remind you to listen tomorrow at seven.
Person: Okay, do that.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.
